title: Fable implementation backlog for Accounting Agent OS 0.1.0
notice: Review output only. Authorises no connection, posting, payment, model call, hosting or policy activation. All example data is fictional. Implement with synthetic data unless a ticket says it waits for client facts.

priority_definitions.P0: Current critical control or correctness defect.
priority_definitions.P1: Foundation change needed before expanding execution or using approved client samples.

ordering: Implement batches in order. Within a batch, follow the order of ticket_ids in the batches list; every dependency of a ticket appears earlier in that order.
general_rules_for_every_ticket: Run make test, make check and the reviewer runner after each ticket.
When a ticket deliberately changes an existing contract or test, record the change and the reason in DECISIONS.md.
Do not weaken an existing blocker to make a case pass.
New blocker and status names proposed here may be renamed, provided the validation cases file is updated in the same change.
Keep handlers pure. New persistence goes through storage.py and new authority checks through service.py.

tickets.title: Enforce review independence with actor kind and artifact contributors
tickets.rationale: Review compares the reviewer only with the enqueuing actor and decides human versus automation by an id prefix. The author of the evidence and the policy can approve their own work through a colleague's run.
affected_files_or_modules: accounting_agent/storage.py (no schema change needed if contributors live in the artifact envelope)
required_behavior: Actor gains kind: 'human' or 'service', set only by trusted transport; the demo worker is 'service', demo preparer and reviewer are 'human'.

At commit, the artifact envelope records contributors: the run actor, the mandate issuer if any, the actor of every source snapshot in the run's input manifest, and the actor who registered the profile version in force.
review() refuses approve and reject unless actor.kind is 'human' and actor.role is 'reviewer', and refuses when actor.id is in contributors. Remove the startswith('worker') test.
Revoke remains available to a human reviewer who is not a contributor.

tickets.title: Separate occurrences from runs; re-dispatch held occurrences; isolate unfit mandates
tickets.rationale: A recurring run held for stale inputs permanently consumes its occurrence, so the scheduled preparation silently never happens. One mandate that no longer fits the client profile makes every tick raise and creates no run for any mandate.
affected_files_or_modules: accounting_agent/storage.py (new occurrences table; move the uniqueness constraint)
required_behavior: New table occurrences(scope, mandate_id, workflow, occurrence_key, status, created) with UNIQUE(mandate_id, workflow, occurrence_key). Status: dispatched, completed, held, awaiting_evidence, skipped_no_catch_up.
Runs reference an occurrence id. More than one run may link to an occurrence, but at most one may complete.
When a mandate run is held for stale inputs, the next tick or the next input change re-dispatches a new run for the same occurrence against current inputs, provided the mandate is still valid.
Each tick writes skipped_no_catch_up rows for occurrences between the previous tick and the current occurrence.
tick evaluates each mandate independently. A control error for one mandate marks that mandate held with a reason, writes an audit event, and the loop continues. The clock still advances.
acceptance_criteria: FV-RC01 and FV-RC02 report FIXED; FV-RC03 still passes.

tickets.title: Introduce accounting periods as records with status; bind runs and sources to a period
tickets.rationale: The period is one mutable field on the client profile. Locking it voids the approvals it should protect, and moving to the next month strands the previous one. The planned November capture and December validation cannot be represented.
affected_files_or_modules: accounting_agent/http.py and web/ (period selector, lock action)
fixtures and tests that rely on profile.period
required_behavior: New table periods(scope, period_id, start, end, status, changed_by, changed_at, reason) with an append-only status history. Status: open, in_review, locked.

Service operations open_period, lock_period and reopen_period, each audited. In this slice they require a human reviewer-role actor who is not the preparer of work in that period; the real authority comes from T-09.
Remove period from the profile schema. Every run is enqueued for a period_id and handlers receive that period in context.

Each dated source is assigned to the period containing its accounting date. An item dated in a different open period than the run is reported once under its own period, not as OUTSIDE_PERIOD in another.
Locking changes status only: it does not bump the client generation or invalidate anything.
Enqueue is refused for a locked period. A new or revised source dated in a locked period is stored and raises LATE_ACTIVITY_IN_LOCKED_PERIOD against that period.

tickets.title: One governing artifact per item and a decision state machine
tickets.rationale: Recurring runs on unchanged inputs create additional current copies of the same item, which can then carry conflicting decisions. A single artifact accepts repeated approvals, and a later approval overrides another reviewer's rejection.
affected_files_or_modules: accounting_agent/storage.py (artifact_runs link table; decisions unchanged and append-only)
required_behavior: The artifact envelope references dependency content hashes, not artifact row ids, so identical inputs give an identical artifact hash across runs.
At commit, when a current artifact with the same scope, workflow, item key and hash exists, link the run to it instead of inserting a copy.
The governing artifact for (scope, workflow, period, item key) is the newest from a completed run. review() refuses approve and reject on any other artifact with 409.

Decision state per artifact: pending to approved or rejected; approved to revoked. Repeating the current state returns 409. A contrary decision by a different reviewer is recorded and sets the state to disputed; disputed is not approved and needs an explicit resolution decision.
state and export report one review state per item plus full history.

tickets.title: Policy approval lifecycle: proposed versions, second-person approval, effective-dated rules
tickets.rationale: The preparer registers and thereby activates the profile that constrains the preparer. There is no proposed state, approver, effective date or supersession, and no way to keep a one-item correction from becoming a rule.
affected_files_or_modules: accounting_agent/service.py (onboard, new propose_rule, approve_rule, reject_rule, context)
accounting_agent/storage.py (policy_rules and rule_decisions tables; authority_grants table)
accounting_agent/modules.py (handlers receive only approved, in-window rules)
accounting_agent/config/ (split demo profile into identity, chart and rules)
web/ (knowledge view shows status and approver)
required_behavior: Step 1: a registered profile version is 'proposed'. approve_profile_version by a human other than the proposer moves the client pointer. Runs use only the approved version.

Step 2: vendor mappings, receipt and matching policy, and close checklist become individually versioned rule records with status (proposed, approved, rejected, superseded), effective_from, effective_to, supersedes, proposed_by, approved_by, evidence references and scope (single_item or reusable). Schema: review section 7.2.
Handlers receive approved rules whose effective window contains the item's accounting date.
A service actor or model output can create a proposed rule only.
authority_grants records who may review, disposition, approve rules, approve mandates, finalize and lock, with effective dates; synthetic grants are labelled as such.
acceptance_criteria: A proposed version or rule is never applied by a run.
The proposer cannot approve; a service actor cannot approve.
A rule effective on the first day of the next period is not applied to an item dated in the current period.
After supersession, re-preparing an earlier period applies the rule that was in force for that date.
Export shows, for every artifact, the rule ids and versions applied.

tickets.title: Bind standing mandates to an approver, a period rule, policy versions and evidence freshness
tickets.rationale: Mandates are issued, ticked and revoked by the preparer role and know nothing about the period they prepare, the policy in force or whether new evidence exists.
required_behavior: A mandate is created as proposed and becomes active only when approved by a human with the approve_mandate grant who is not the issuer.

Mandate stores period_rule (which period each occurrence prepares), the rule versions it was approved against, a freshness predicate (required source kinds with as_of on or after the occurrence start) and a mandatory expiry.
A change to a bound rule moves the mandate to needs_reconfirmation and stops dispatch.
An occurrence whose freshness predicate is not met is recorded as awaiting_evidence and is dispatched when the evidence arrives within the mandate window.
acceptance_criteria: Issuer cannot approve own mandate.

tickets.title: Source lifecycle: ordering, removal and supersession
tickets.rationale: The last write is the current version, so a delayed older batch replaces newer data. Feed removals cannot be represented, and a supersedes link produces only a blocker.
required_behavior: Source envelope gains as_of (source timestamp or feed sequence) and keeps source_system.
A version with an older as_of than the current one is stored as history and does not become current.
A tombstone removes a source from the current population with a reason (feed_removed, voided, superseded) and keeps history.
supersedes is resolved by the engine: the superseded row leaves the population and the link is kept on both records.
Revision or removal of a source that has an approved governing artifact raises an exception against that approval.
acceptance_criteria: Probe P07: the newer amount stays current after the late older batch.
A tombstoned pending authorisation produces no artifact and no blockers.

tickets.title: Statement-based completeness control
tickets.rationale: The control is a count and one signed total declared in the same intake as the population. It excludes foreign-currency and out-of-period rows silently, passes on substitution, sums payments with purchases and has no balances to chain.
required_behavior: New source kind statement: account, statement id, cycle start and end, opening balance, closing balance, totals by activity type (purchases, credits, payments, fees, interest), line count, optional line ids, provenance (system_extract or manually_keyed, and the supplying actor).
Checks: opening equals the prior statement's closing; opening plus activity equals closing; intake population by activity type equals statement totals for the cycle.
Rows excluded from the tie (other currency, outside the cycle, pending) are listed in an unreconciled_population section of a per-account package artifact.
Line-level tie when line ids are supplied.
A sign convention is declared per source system and validated; payments and purchases are never summed in one direction.
acceptance_criteria: A foreign-currency row appears as an unreconciled population item (FV-C19 extended).
An opening-balance break blocks every item on that account.

tickets.title: Exceptions and dispositions as records; blocker propagation between steps
tickets.rationale: A blocker is a string with no resolution path, so duplicates, credits, splits, payments and foreign charges can never be completed. Upstream blockers do not affect downstream steps.
affected_files_or_modules: accounting_agent/service.py (commit opens exceptions; new disposition and revoke_disposition; context passes dispositions)
accounting_agent/modules.py (handlers consume dispositions; Step declares propagation)
required_behavior: commit opens one exception row per (item, code) and supersedes it when a later governing artifact no longer has that code.

disposition() records a choice from a closed vocabulary per code, with evidence references, reason, deciding human and scope (single_item by default). Vocabulary and example: review sections 5 (F-10) and 7.2.
A disposition is an immutable input in the item's manifest. Re-preparation applies it and cites it in the artifact; the result then needs independent review.
Only humans with the matching grant may disposition. scope propose_rule creates a proposed rule and nothing else.
Each Step declares whether dependency blockers propagate; package-level codes propagate by default.
acceptance_criteria: Two duplicate candidates with a distinct_purchases disposition and distinct receipts become eligible and cite the disposition.

An inventory step with NO_SOURCE_EVIDENCE blocks its dependants.

validate_entry is the single place for balance, line shape, account, period and currency checks.
An eligible card proposal carries its derived entry (debit proposed category, credit the card's liability account).
One source item may originate at most one live entry in a book; a second raises SOURCE_ALREADY_HAS_ENTRY on both.
The artifact envelope binds entity, book and period.

tickets.title: Finalize a reviewed period package
tickets.rationale: Review status is recomputed on every read, so nothing can be handed over as the reviewed package for a period.
required_behavior: finalize_package(period, workflow) by a human with the finalize grant writes an immutable record: governing artifact ids and hashes, decisions, dispositions, manifest, rule versions, open exceptions and audit chain head.
Finalization is refused while any item is disputed or any package-level blocker is open; open item-level exceptions are listed explicitly and require an acknowledgement reason.
Later changes never alter a finalized package; they raise POST_FINALIZATION_CHANGE referencing it.
Export of a finalized package is byte-stable apart from export metadata.

tickets.title: Failure classification, backoff, lease heartbeat and a worker that survives errors
tickets.rationale: Every failure is retried immediately up to three times, a handler slower than the lease can never commit, and the demo worker thread stops permanently on any exception.
required_behavior: Classify failures: transient (retry with stored backoff), deterministic (fail at once with a visible reason), stale (hold).
Lease heartbeat extends a valid lease; commit still requires the token and current inputs.
The worker loop records an error and continues; health reports the last error.
A held run has an explicit outcome: superseded by a named newer run, or resumed.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic handler error consumes one attempt.
A long handler with heartbeat commits.
The worker continues after an injected database-lock error.
tickets.human_decision_required: None.

tickets.title: Export consistency and audit anchoring
tickets.rationale: The export reads state and history in two transactions and hashes its own timestamp, and the audit chain has no reference outside the database, so truncation is undetectable.
required_behavior: Read the whole export in one transaction.
content_hash covers content only; export metadata is hashed separately.
Every export and finalized package records the audit chain head and length; verify_audit can check a database against a previously exported head.
state returns paged audit; export returns all.
acceptance_criteria: Two exports of unchanged state have the same content_hash.
Deleting the last audit row in a copy is detected against an earlier export.
tickets.human_decision_required: None. External retention is a hosted-stage decision.

tickets.title: Currency contract: validated codes and minor units
tickets.rationale: Two-decimal money and free-text currency sit in the shared core. Adequate for the USD fixture; wrong for the first other currency.
required_behavior: Currency must be an upper-case ISO 4217 code from a bundled table with its minor unit.
money(value, currency) validates the number of decimals for that currency.
Foreign items stay held; add optional explicit fields for original amount, original currency, rate, rate source and rate date so a later disposition can use them.
acceptance_criteria: 'usd' is rejected at intake.
